title: Bengaluru Pink Line Opens to Crowds, Roses and Doubts Over Partial Route
excerpt: The 7.5-km Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere stretch cut a 20-to-30-minute road trip to about 10 minutes on day one, but commuters say the unfinished underground section still leaves cross-city journeys fragmented.
body:
• Public services on Bengaluru's Pink Line began at 6 a.m. on Saturday on the 7.5-km elevated stretch between Kalena Agrahara and Suddagunte Palya (Tavarekere), a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated it.
  • Six stations are open — Kalena Agrahara, Hulimavu, IIM Bangalore, JP Nagar 4th Phase, Jayadeva Hospital and Suddagunte Palya/Tavarekere — with Jayadeva Hospital providing an interchange with the Yellow Line.
  • First riders were welcomed with pink roses by minister Krishna Byre Gowda, and commuters said a journey that took 20 to 30 minutes by road took about nine to 10 minutes by metro.
  • The scepticism is about what is not open: the 13.8-km underground section is still under construction, so many cross-city trips still need multiple interchanges.
Launched, partially operating: As of November 14, 2026, only the 7.5-km elevated stretch of the Pink Line is carrying passengers. The full line toward MG Road and Nagawara is not yet operating, and no fare figure is stated in the reports this article is based on — check the fare at the station before travelling.

The first public train on Bengaluru's Pink Line left at 6 a.m. on Saturday, opening the Bannerghatta Road corridor to metro travel after a wait residents put at three to four years, according to IANS. Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda handed pink roses to the first riders at Kalena Agrahara and rode with commuters to SG Palya, while several passengers and metro staff wore pink for the launch.

The first-day experience

For residents along Bannerghatta Road — a corridor IANS describes as one of the city's worst traffic-affected stretches, home to hundreds of technology companies — the immediate gain was time. Commuters told IANS that travelling between stations on the congested road had taken 20 to 30 minutes, against about nine to 10 minutes by metro.

Reporting by Urban Acres, drawing on Times of India interviews, found the same relief at street level. Pallavi Ramnathkar, a homemaker, said her nearest station is now about 200 metres from home, compared with travelling 1.5 to 2 km to reach a metro station before. Veena Basavaraj said residents had previously depended on private vehicles, buses or ride-hailing even for short trips.

"Took the first ride on Pink Line of Namma Metro. First train started at sharp 6 a.m. It was flawless and smooth."

— Krishna Byre Gowda, Bengaluru Development Minister, on social media

Where the scepticism comes from

The doubts are not about the trains that ran on Saturday. They are about the partial opening. The 13.8-km underground section of the Pink Line is still under construction, so a trip from south Bengaluru toward MG Road or Whitefield can still require changing at Jayadeva Hospital to the Yellow Line, at RV Road to the Green Line and at Majestic to the Purple Line, as commuters explained in reporting carried by Vijaya Chronicle. Sunitha K., a commuter from Bilekahalli, said RV Road station is already short on platform space and could become more crowded than Majestic at peak hours.

Urban Acres reported a version of the same concern from the road: traffic remained heavy near Vega City during peak hours, and residents Baby Shalini and Anasuya A called for the line to be extended further south toward Bannerghatta so more commuters benefit. A BMRCL official told Vijaya Chronicle that passenger movement and crowd levels at RV Road would be monitored, with crowd-management measures where required.

Byre Gowda said efforts would continue to operationalise the Pink Line up to MG Road and then Nagawara, according to IANS.

Service details from the launch reports

The open stretch covers six stations: Kalena Agrahara, Hulimavu, IIM Bangalore, JP Nagar 4th Phase, Jayadeva Hospital and Suddagunte Palya/Tavarekere. IANS reported the operating pattern as follows: on Mondays the first train departs Kalena Agrahara at 4.55 a.m. and Suddagunte Palya/Tavarekere at 5 a.m.; from Tuesday to Saturday services begin at 6 a.m. from both ends; on Sundays the first trains start at 7 a.m. The last train departs Kalena Agrahara at 10.50 p.m. and Suddagunte Palya/Tavarekere at 10.54 p.m. Trains run every eight minutes at peak hours from Monday to Saturday, every 10 minutes off-peak, and every 10 minutes on Saturdays and Sundays.

Before planning your trip

  • Only the Kalena Agrahara to Suddagunte Palya/Tavarekere stretch is open — the Pink Line does not yet run to MG Road or Nagawara.
  • Cross-city trips may still need interchanges at Jayadeva Hospital, RV Road and Majestic; allow extra time at peak hours.
  • No fare for the new stretch was stated in the launch reports — confirm it at the station before travelling.
  • First and last train times differ by day; check the pattern above before setting out.

nri_angle: Bannerghatta Road is home to many of Bengaluru's technology workers, including returning NRIs, for whom the corridor's commute has been a daily cost of living in the city.
